judgment_on_surviving_mutant: Q3-failing-check-reported-as-passing: the stated reason holds, and I re-established it with my own hand rather than the executor's. Mutating CommandChecker so a started-and-failed check reports exit 0 leaves the routed suite untouched (PASS, 33/33) because the production writer's refusal ends every CLI run before a failing check can drive a repair and no routed check is engineered to fail-after-starting; the same mutation is killed by the unit layer (TestCheckThatFailsIsCapturedAsAnExitCode FAILs). It is a real coverage gap of the routed face, honestly recorded, expected-to-survive before it was observed, and it closes itself when the write route lands; I do not consider it blocking for this card, whose own disclosure already binds that repair leg to the out-of-scope domain route.
